report.summary: The change does what the request describes. protectedFileHashes now treats a SandboxFileError ENOENT from Files.readFile as an absent file (null), like the existing 404 branch. Any other readFile failure still fails with RUN_ACCESS_VIOLATION and the same message, with no path or secret in it. The guard is no weaker: an agent that creates a missing login file changes its hash from null to a value, and one that deletes a protected file changes it from a value to null, so both runs still fail. The new Worker case checks the observable result (the run completes with no error code), and the existing changed-file case still covers the failure path. The issues.test.tsx fix waits for page 2 to replace page 1 instead of sleeping or retrying, and its assertions are unchanged. node_modules is not installed in this worktree, so I could not read SandboxFileError.is in @cloudflare/sandbox 1.0.0 and did not run the tests. There are no blocking findings.

findings.text: The test throws a plain Error with name 'SandboxFileError' and code 'ENOENT' added, not a real SandboxFileError. That proves the fix only if SandboxFileError.is in @cloudflare/sandbox 1.0.0 checks the name or a brand rather than instanceof. If it uses instanceof, this case fails, while production, which gets real instances, would still work. node_modules is missing here, so I could not confirm which. Consider building the error with the SDK's own constructor so the test does not depend on how .is works inside the SDK.

Treating ENOENT as absent extends the existing 404 path, so I see no spec conflict. Docs 01 and 08 describe the guard only as comparing hashes, so this is not new behavior. The PR could still add a short line to docs/IMPLEMENTATION_NOTES.md noting that a missing protected file hashes as null, so the choice is recorded.
